Subject: Cedara inference needs: dedicated capacity + burst plan

Alex —

Thanks for the demo this morning. To summarize our current ask from Platform: we need a dedicated pool to serve our long-context NLU workloads (primarily a 16k-token LLM family plus a trimmed 8k variant for lighter queries). Key SLOs and traffic shape below:

- Sustained baseline: ~1,200 tokens/sec (aggregate across endpoints) during business hours (US-PDT).
- Peak bursts: periodic batch jobs and inference spikes up to ~6,000 tokens/sec for ~10–20 minute windows (1–2x per day).
- P95 tail target for interactive endpoints: <= 250 ms (generation latency per request).
- Model mix: 70% long-context 16k Llama3-ish quantized model (perf similar to Llama3-32k @ 16k), 30% 8k trimmed variant.
- Cold-start constraints: we have cold shards when deployments roll; KV warmup matters; need graceful degradation not hard failures.

Questions: can Redwood guarantee the p95 with dedicated capacity? What does committed slab look like (GPUs, headroom) and how should we price/commit? Also want a short mutual action plan to get from POC -> reserved.

Jordan

Alex / Kim —

Quick sizing sketch below (assumptions first, then math and recommendation). I attached a one-sheet calc (cedara_capacity_calc.xlsx).

Assumptions
- Model family: Llama3-16k equivalent (quantized 4-bit runtime). Performance: measured on our bench: 2.4k tokens/sec per H100 @ latency target for greedy generation for a 16k-ish working context when batching is active. 8k trimmed variant: ~3.6k tokens/sec per H100 (higher throughput due to shorter context).
- KV cache hit rate: baseline 85% (warm), during roll or cold-start assume 25% hit rate first 5 minutes until warmed.
- Typical interactive request size: prompt 120 tokens, generation 160 tokens => 280 tokens/request average for interactive endpoints.
- Batch jobs: large batched inference (avg 1,200 tokens/request) with high batching efficiency (amortizes attention kernels).
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive; we budget p95 budget to require a per-request processing latency target that translates into tokens/sec headroom.
- Safety headroom target: 35% above expected peak to allow margin for KV churn / misestimation.

Math (simplified)
1) Convert tokens/sec requirement to equivalent H100s (steady-state):
   - Baseline tokens/sec required = 1,200 t/s.
   - Weighted per-GPU throughput (mix): 70% @ 2.4k t/s + 30% @ 3.6k t/s => weighted average per-GPU throughput = 0.7*2400 + 0.3*3600 = 1680 + 1080 = 2760 t/s per H100 under warm conditions (with batching).
   - Required GPUs (baseline) = ceil(1,200 / 2,760) = 1 GPU. (Note: this is an optimistic packing number assuming even distribution and full batching.)

2) Account for burst windows and real-world inefficiencies (KV cold, cross-model fragmentation, tail latency):
   - Peak needed = 6,000 t/s.
   - GPUs to serve peak (warm state) = ceil(6,000 / 2,760) = 3 GPUs.

3) Apply safety headroom (35%):
   - Baseline commit = 1 * 1.35 => 1.35 => round up to 2 GPUs for practical capacity allocation.
   - Peak/burst cushion = 3 * 1.35 => 4.05 => round up to 5 GPUs (we recommend rounding conservatively given tail risk).

4) Cold-start and KV warmup consideration:
   - During first 5 minutes, effective per-GPU throughput drops roughly ~40% (from KV misses + cache repopulation). For a 6,000 t/s spike, that could require double the GPU count transiently if relying solely on warm throughput.

Recommendation
- Committed slab: 3 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (this gives a predictable baseline and simplifies placement of long-context shards). Rationale: 3 gives steady baseline coverage and reduces risk of under-provisioning when fragmentation occurs across model variants.
- Shared burst pool: 2 additional burst GPUs (pre-warmed H100s) available to Cedara when spikes hit (total available = 5). These are billed at burst rate when used.
- Canary plan: Ramp to 50% traffic on committed slab for first 72 hours, run warmup scripts to prime KV caches, then move to 10% shared-burst usage for first week.
- Operational notes: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for session affinity; warm-up hooks via prefetch for scheduled batch jobs; add auto-warm scripts triggered on commit/failover.

Cost/commercial suggestion for Kim
- Option A (12-month commit): 3 reserved H100-equivalent + 2 optional burst GPUs. Discounted unit price for reserved; burst billed at premium.
- Option B (3-month pilot): 2 reserved H100-equivalent + 3 burst GPUs (higher burst reliance), higher per-token rates; option to convert leftover burst to reserved within 30 days with pro-rated credits.

Caveats and next steps
- The per-GPU tokens/sec numbers above assume our 4-bit optimized kernels and a batching efficiency consistent with your job shape. If Cedara's traffic is substantially more asynchronous (many small single-request streams) the effective per-GPU throughput could drop 30–50%.
- If you prefer a lower commit, we can propose a placement that relies more on regional cross-pool borrowing, but that weakens SLA guarantees.

Attaching: cedara_capacity_calc.xlsx (detailed sheet with sensitivity rows: KV hit 25%/50%/85%, quantization perf +/- 15%, batch efficiency +/- 30%).

Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute sync to walk through the numbers.

—Priyom
